1.. Parking & Outdoor Dining in a Post Pandemic World  -  Action: agenda title only {\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 City Manager Chi introduced Director of Community Development Ursula Luna-Reynosa who presented a PowerPoint communication titled Parking & Outdoor Dining in a Post-Pandemic World with slides entitled: March 15 H Item, Parking and Transportation, Every Parking System, Two Primary Patterns of Settlement in California, Conventional Post-1945 Design Approach, How are parking ratios determined?, Conventional Parking Requirements, Typical Office Parking, Form follows parking requirements, Cost to meet requirements using parking structures, How much revenue needed, Conventional Development, Mixed Use, Park Once District, Park Once Case Study - Palo Alto, Removing Minimum Parking - Examples, Parking is Local(2), HB Shared Parking Program Examples, Next Steps Short-Term, Next Steps Long-Term, and Questions.\par
\par
Councilmember Posey stated there is a lot of un-utilized real estate and he sees the need for more centralized and practical parking plans that consider the current and expected change in modes of transportation such as Uber, Lyft, increased bicycle use and people walking in certain areas.   Councilmember Posey and staff discussed ways to secure funding for parking consultants such as Southern California Association of Government (SCAG) grants.\par
\par
Councilmember Kalmick suggested using Covid funds to speed up the study process and allow property owners options for best use of their parking space.  There was discussion on how code could be changed with sufficient details so that each situation would not require hiring a transportation consultant, and include notification to surrounding neighbors who would be affected, keeping the option for reciprocal agreements, and consider how parking requirements change as business types change.\par
\par
Mayor Pro Tem Delgleize and staff discussed issues related to areas where residents and shoppers have different parking needs at different times of the day, and clarified that Code cannot dictate options for private property owners such as retail parking spaces must be made available for area residents after business hours.  However, Code does not prohibit a property owner from making such an agreement with residents who live within 250 feet of the property.\par
\par
Councilmember Peterson and Director Luna-Reynosa discussed changes in tenants does trigger a notification to the City through the Certificate of Occupancy process, and Councilmember Peterson stated that examples from cities that have public transportation options should not be used because our area does not have good public transportation. \par
\par
There was clarification regarding the Second Block Downtown Temporary Use Permit which is in effect through Labor Day.  After Labor Day that street will be reopened and not be kept closed until Council has the opportunity to consider zoning code changes.\par
\par
Councilmember Peterson reminded everyone that the Downtown area is within the Coastal Zone and has unique regulations to be considered.\par
\par
Councilmember Moser concurred with Councilmember Peterson regarding using areas with good public transportation options do not make good examples for Huntington Beach, and suggested environmental and sustainability measures be considered, and maintaining the Planning Commission appeal process in case reality differs from intention.\par
\par
Mayor Carr and Director Luna-Reynosa discussed lesser fees would be related to the administrative process for a shared parking program since that does not go to Planning Commission. \par
\par
Mayor Carr and Director Luna-Reynosa discussed designing for outdoor dining could be more problematic as it needs to be site specific, and would need to provide basics while allowing for flexibility and creativity. \par
\par
Mayor Carr stated her support for developing a comprehensive Master Parking Plan utilizing the SCAG grant, including a shared parking program which includes an inexpensive appeal process.\par
\par
Councilmember Peterson shared his observation in most cities that bike considerations are needed only in certain areas, such as Downtown and beach areas for Huntington Beach, not throughout the City.\par
\par
Councilmember Posey stated another issue that needs to be addressed looking forward is parking for housing units that are over-occupied, as well as planning for bike considerations in specific corridors.\par
\par
Mayor Carr thanked staff for the great presentation, good Study Session, and confirmed with Director Luna-Reynosa staff understands how Council would like to move forward.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 City Manager Chi introduced Community & Library Services Director Chris Slama and Police Chief Julian Harvey who jointly presented a Power Point presentation titled "Consideration of Proposed Pilot Concert Program - Pacific Airshow" with slides entitled: Background, Current Live Entertainment Protocols, State Beach Concerts, City Council Direction, Staff Assessment To Date, Pilot Concert Program Option Identified, Event Permitting Consideration, Staff Recommendation, Questions?\par
\par
Delgleize: typical summer event day (i.e US open)  how many people on beach - appx 20-30k/day.  Second festival by Code 4 (Air Show company) - nothing until how successful that turns out.  This would be only pilot concert.  Chief Harvey - commented on 12,000 max/ more people in area due to openness. \par
\par
Peterson - Chief Harvey discussed options and challenges to an open outside concert.  Questioned $5 administration fee - itemized list and settle after the fact? Code 4 gets billed the day of event for security.  Feels give fees up front to vendor if possible.\par
\par
Posey - also concerned about $5 fee, especially since Air Show nets a high dollar amount to city - double dipping?  Parking surcharges, any estimate how many Air Show attendees will stay for concert. Additional Permit cost. Tremendous benefit to the city in addition to risk. How reconcile $5 for concert vs. US Open which is all free, with staff/security being same.  City Manager Chi assured any overcharges would be refunded to vendor.  Support with one provision - fair in cost recovery, easy for businesses to operate in HB - transparent accounting and reconciliation within 60 days.\par
\par
Carr - fees are typically a pass through fee,  Feels they are warranted for this type of event.  Feels it is smart to start small with a pilot program and later expand\par
\par
Peterson - support all RA's except "D" - $5 fee\par
\par
Delgleize would like fee renamed\par
}
